chunk_findings.detail: The tab fix is incomplete: `format_baseline` is unchanged and still writes raw TAB-separated fields, while `parse_baseline` reads the baseline with `text.splitlines()`. A POSIX path may contain a newline (or any other `splitlines()` line boundary). If `scan()` records a site for a file named `ddflow/a\nb.py`, `format_baseline` emits `program\tgit\tddflow/a\nb.py\t1`; `parse_baseline` then sees the first physical line `program\tgit\tddflow/a`, attempts `rest.rsplit("\t", 1)`, and raises `ValueError`. The new API ratchet path calls `I.parse_baseline(committed.read_text())` without catching this, so a valid filesystem name can make the interface view fail. The added round-trip test covers an embedded tab but not a line-boundary character, so the earlier “fixed” claim does not cover this case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces.py:parse_baseline (line 136)

chunk_findings.detail: The new URL guard is applied only to the `MANAGED_NAMES` managed-file rule. The separate `.git/hooks` managed-file rule is still executed unconditionally after `_URL.match(v)`. Given the literal `"https://example.com/.git/hooks/pre-commit"`, `_URL.match` succeeds and the scanner records `network host:example.com`, but `"/" + GIT_HOOKS in v` is also true, so it additionally records a local `managed-file` dependency for `.git/hooks`. A URL path component is not a local file owned by another tool, so this is a false interface site and the ratchet can fail on it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_literal_site

chunk_findings.detail: `programs_of` splits shell-string literals on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, and newline without respecting shell quoting or escapes. Given `os.system("git commit -m 'fix && bug'")`, the scanner splits inside the quoted commit message and adds a second program site derived from `bug'` (or `bug` after `_base` strips the quote), even though the shell runs only `git`. The same happens for regex-like arguments such as `grep -E 'a|b'`, where `b'` becomes a program family. This creates arbitrary false program dependencies from ordinary quoted arguments and can make the external-interface ratchet fail on false positives.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:programs_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new top-level guard admits any dotted call ending in `.joinpath`, but the recursive `flat` helper only admits calls whose dotted name is in `_PATH_CTORS`. For input `p.joinpath(".git", p.joinpath("hooks"))`, the outer call passes because `name.endswith(".joinpath")`, but when `flat` processes the second argument it sees an `ast.Call` with dotted name `p.joinpath`, which is not in the fixed `_PATH_CTORS` set, so it appends `None` instead of recursing into the `"hooks"` constant. The flattened fragments for the outer call become `[".git", None]`, not `[".git", "hooks"]`, and the nested call visited separately only contributes `["hooks"]`; therefore no `.git/hooks` managed-file site is emitted. This is a false negative introduced by the path-constructor restriction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_git_hooks_join

chunk_findings.detail: The new test asserts that the scanner must emit **no** interface sites for any file whose module is in `I.SELF_MODULES`, i.e. it enforces a whole-module exclusion, not just exclusion of the scanner’s pattern-table constants. Given a real external interface inside a self module, for example adding `subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], ...)` or `os.environ["DDFLOW_ARCH_BASELINE"]` to `ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py`, `I.scan(ROOT)` will suppress those sites because the module is self-excluded, and this test still passes. The ratchet can therefore report “no grew/shrank” while an external CLI/environment interface in the census module itself is uncounted, defeating the stated goal of proving “every external interface goes through its adapter.” The pattern-table strings should be filtered by node/context, not by excluding all call sites in the module.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous tab-round-trip issue is only partly fixed. `parse_baseline` now uses `raw.split("\t", 2)` and `rest.rsplit("\t", 1)`, which handles an embedded tab, but the baseline format still writes the path field verbatim and `parse_baseline` still iterates `text.splitlines()`. A valid POSIX path such as `ddflow/foo\nbar.py` is therefore written with a literal newline inside the path; reading that committed baseline splits it into a separate record, and `_interfaces` then raises `ValueError` from `raw.split("\t", 2)` on the path fragment. chunk_findings.detail: `parse_baseline` tries to skip comment lines with `not raw.startswith("#")`, but it checks before stripping leading whitespace. Given a baseline text containing an indented comment line such as `"  # header"`, `raw.strip()` is true yet `raw.startswith("#")` is false, so the code proceeds to `kind, family, path, n = raw.split("\t")`. That line has no tab, so `raw.split("\t")` returns a one-element list and the four-way unpack raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (got 1, expected 4)`. A comment at column 0 is correctly ignored, but an indented comment crashes the entire parser.

For `os.system("git status > /dev/null 2>&1")`, the scanner records a bogus `program` site for family `1`, a false external interface that can make the ratchet fail on code that only redirects file descriptors.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The test is presented as the safety argument for excluding `I.SELF_MODULES` from the interface census, but it only checks static import families. The interface census counts managed-file literals without requiring an import (for example `g = "AGENTS.md"` is counted in `test_managed_files_exclude_prose_and_comments`). If someone adds `open("AGENTS.md").read()` to `ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py`, the interface census will suppress the resulting site because the module is self-excluded, while `A.scan(ROOT)` gains no `subprocess`, `http`, `shutil`, `clock-env`, `sqlite3`, or `fsio` importer for that module because `open` is a builtin. `test_the_census_modules_import_no_os_family` and `test_the_census_does_not_count_its_own_pattern_tables` therefore still pass even though an external managed-file interface has been hidden from the census.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:test_the_census_modules_import_no_os_family

chunk_findings.detail: The prose exclusion is broken: `self.prose = {id(n.value) ...}` stores the identity of the string value, but both `file_protocols` and the `ast.Constant` branch test `id(node) not in self.prose`, the identity of the AST node. Those two IDs are never equal. A docstring `"""https://example.com"""` therefore reaches `_literal_site` and emits `network host:example.com`, and a docstring exactly `"tools/list"` still leaks into `file_protocols`. This is previous finding 6 still present, not fixed by the cited probe.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_Scan.__init__ / _Scan.run

`_SHELL_OPS` contains `"
"`, but `shlex.shlex(..., whitespace_split=True)` consumes newline as whitespace, so `"
"` is never returned as a token. For `os.system("git status
pre-commit run")`, the token list is `["git", "status", "pre-commit", "run"]`; `_shell_commands` returns only `["git"]`, so `pre-commit` is run but not recorded. This underreports a newline-separated external program.

chunk_findings.detail: `shutil.which("git")` is recorded as a `program` site, but `shutil.which` only locates an executable; it does not run it. Given `if shutil.which("git"): ...` with no subprocess call, the scanner emits `program git`, a false dependency that can make the arch guard fail even though no git process is ever run.

chunk_findings.detail: `_git_hooks_join` flattens every `ast.Div` BinOp without requiring a path constructor. Valid code with a user-defined `__truediv__` such as `NonPath() / ".git" / "hooks"` leaves `[None, ".git", "hooks"]`, so `pairwise` finds `(".git", "hooks")` and emits a `managed-file` site for `.git/hooks` although no local path is constructed. This false positive can fail the arch guard.

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `I.scan(ROOT)` completes in under 15 seconds of wall-clock time. This makes the suite fail based on machine load, disk speed, or CI virtualization even when the scanner's performance has not regressed and the change is correct. For example, on a shared or throttled CI worker with a cold page cache, the full-repository parse and scan can exceed 15 s, causing a spurious failure unrelated to scanner behavior.

chunk_findings.detail:
The newline fix splits the raw shell line on `
` before shlex, so it treats newlines that are not shell command separators as separators. For `subprocess.run("cat <<EOF
git status
EOF", shell=True)`, the heredoc body line `git status` is lexed with `fresh=True`, so `pre-commit`-style logic records `git` as an external program even though the shell only passes that text to `cat`; this creates a bogus `program` interface. The same split also mis-handles shell line continuation: `subprocess.run("git status \
pre-commit run", shell=True)` is one `git` command with `pre-commit` as an argument, but the scanner records `pre-commit` as a separate command. Conversely, `subprocess.run("git commit -m 'line1
line2' && pre-commit run", shell=True)` makes the first split line unbalanced for shlex; the function returns after `git` and never sees the real `pre-commit` command. Thus the census can both invent and miss external interfaces for multi-line shell strings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: `shlex(..., punctuation_chars=True)` tokenizes parentheses as separate tokens, but `_SHELL_OPS` does not treat `(` or `)` as command boundaries. For `subprocess.run("(git status)", shell=True)`, the token stream begins with `(`; because `fresh` is true, `_shell_commands` returns `(` as a program and then ignores `git` since `fresh` is now false. If unknown tokens are counted, the ratchet sees a bogus external program `(`; if unknown tokens are filtered, the real `git` dependency is missed. This is wrong for a shell line where the actual external command inside the subshell is `git`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The new `literals=False` path suppresses every string-literal interface kind in census modules, not only their pattern tables. The added test demonstrates the suppression directly: in `services/archifaces_scan.py`, `X = "AGENTS.md"` produces no `managed-file` site (only the `env`/`REAL` call site is kept), while the same literal in `services/real.py` is counted. Therefore, if a census module contains a real literal interface—e.g. `AGENTS = "AGENTS.md"` later used to read the file, a default protocol method literal, or a default URL host—the interface census omits it solely because the module is in `I.SELF_MODULES`. The delta only proves that env call sites survive; real literal interfaces inside census modules remain invisible to the ratchet, so the previous self-exclusion hole is not fully answered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:sites_in

chunk_findings.detail: The new `literals=False` mode is meant to hide the census modules' own pattern tables, but it suppresses every string-literal interface kind in those modules, including a genuine `managed-file` use. The new probe in `tests/test_arch_interfaces.py::test_the_census_does_not_count_its_own_pattern_tables` only proves an `env` call survives for a self module; it does not exercise the previous managed-file scenario. Given `ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py` containing `open("AGENTS.md").read()`, that module is in `I.SELF_MODULES` and is scanned with `literals=False`, so the `AGENTS.md` managed-file literal is omitted, `I.scan(ROOT)` reports no site, and the arch guard can pass even though a census module reaches a managed file directly. This is previous finding 3 still present: the fix/probe does not answer the suppressed-managed-file path, only the suppressed-call path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:sites_in literals=False

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_unquoted_newlines_to_semicolons` removes newlines before shlex, but the lexer is still constructed with shlex's default `commenters = '#'`. Given `os.system("ls # comment\ngit status")`, the helper produces `ls # comment ; git status`; shlex treats everything from `#` to the end of the string as a comment, so `_shell_commands` returns only `ls` and the scanner omits the `git` program. In a real shell the comment ends at the newline and `git status` runs, so this underreports an external interface.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The helper treats any unquoted newline as a command separator, but a backslash-newline outside quotes is a shell line continuation, not a separator. For the shell string produced by `os.system("git \\\nstatus")` (characters `git \` newline `status`), the helper changes it to `git \ ; status`; `_shell_commands` then sees `;` as an operator and returns both `git` and `status`. The shell joins the continuation and runs only `git status`, so the scanner emits a false `program status` dependency.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_unquoted_newlines_to_semicolons

chunk_findings.detail: The manual comment state introduced by `lex.commenters = ""` ends a comment at any `;` token, but a semicolon inside a shell comment does not end the comment. Given `os.system("# note ; git status")`, the shell treats the whole line as a comment and runs no program. The scanner tokenizes this as `#`, `note`, `;`, `git`, `status`; the `#` starts its comment state, the `;` ends that state, and `git` is returned as a program family. This creates a false external interface and can make the interface ratchet fail on code that runs nothing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The comment state also starts a comment from any token beginning with `#`, even when the `#` is quoted, and the pre-pass does not know that shell comments ignore quotes. For `os.system('echo "# note" && git status')`, the shell runs `echo` and then `git`, but shlex yields the argument token `# note`; `_shell_commands` enters comment mode there and, because there is no `;` token, never records `git`. For `os.system("# it's\nls")`, the shell comment ends at the newline and runs `ls`, but the helper treats the apostrophe as opening a quote, leaves the newline inside that quote, shlex then sees an unbalanced quote, and the fallback returns only `#`, so `ls` is missed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: `line.replace("\\\n", " ")` removes every backslash-newline pair without counting preceding backslashes, so it treats an escaped backslash followed by a newline as a line continuation. For an unquoted shell string whose value is `git ` followed by two literal backslashes, a newline, and `pre-commit run`, the shell sees `\\` as a literal backslash argument to `git` and the following newline as a command separator, so `pre-commit` runs. The helper replaces the second backslash and newline with a space, removing the separator, so `_shell_commands` returns only `git` and the census misses the `pre-commit` external interface.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_unquoted_newlines_to_semicolons

chunk_findings.detail: `line.replace("\\\n", " ")` is not equivalent to shell line continuation: an unquoted backslash-newline is removed with no inserted separator. For the shell string value `git\<newline>status`, the actual shell command is the single word `gitstatus`, so `git` should not be recorded; this code changes it to `git status`, whose shlex tokens are `["git", "status"]`, and `_shell_commands` returns `["git"]`. That is a false external interface, even though no `git` process is run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_unquoted_newlines_to_semicolons

chunk_findings.detail: The new hand-rolled comment state assumes every dequoted token starting with `#` begins a shell comment, but shlex dequotes arguments. For `os.system('echo "#" && git status')`, shlex produces tokens `echo`, `#`, `&`, `&`, `git`, `status`; the `#` sets `comment=True`, and because `comment` is cleared only by `;`, the subsequent `&& git status` is ignored. The actual shell runs `git` (the `#` was quoted), so the census misses an external program family.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: `archdeps(repo)` default path still returns `"\n".join(lines)`, a plain `str`, even though the function is annotated `-> O.Outcome`; the new `interfaces`/`baseline` branch returns an `O.Outcome`. A caller following the declared contract, e.g. `res = archdeps(repo); res.ok`, works on `archdeps(repo, interfaces="CLI")` but raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'ok'` on the default path, so the API now has two incompatible return types and the interface-census branch is not available through the same contract the default path still exposes. The original bare-string return remains unchanged at line 57.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/arch_deps.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: `parse_baseline` checks `raw.startswith("#")` before stripping whitespace, so an indented comment line such as `" # header"` makes `raw.strip()` truthy but `not raw.startswith("#")` true, and line 141 then calls `json.loads(" # header")`, raising `json.JSONDecodeError` instead of skipping the comment.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces.py:140

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. `self.prose` only exempts `ast.Expr` whose value is a `Constant` string. A standalone f-string such as `f"opencode.json"` is `ast.Expr(ast.JoinedStr)`; its child `Constant(value="opencode.json")` is not in `self.prose`, so `_literal_site` adds `managed-file opencode.json`, contradicting the module’s own guarantee that “a string statement can not produce a hit.” The same issue causes f-string literal entries from `MCP_METHODS`/`ACP_METHODS` to produce protocol hits.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_Scan.__init__:self.prose

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. `_call` reads only `node.args[0]` and ignores `node.keywords`, so valid keyword-call forms such as `subprocess.run(args=["git", "status"])`, `os.getenv(key="FOO")`, `shutil.which(cmd="git")`, and `os.environ.get(key="FOO")` all report family `<dynamic>` even though the program/env name is statically known.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_call

chunk_findings.detail: `shlex.shlex(..., whitespace_split=True)` discards newline characters, so the `"\n"` entry in `_SHELL_OPS` never appears in the token list. For `subprocess.run("git status\nls", shell=True)`, the method returns `["git"]` because `git`, `status`, and `ls` become consecutive tokens and no separator resets `fresh`; `ls` is never recorded as a second command, violating the function’s description that it names the first word of every command in a shell line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: Every line in this committed baseline is a Python/JSON-style list literal (for example `["env", "<all>", "ddflow/api/briefing.py", 1]`) with no tab separators. `ddflow/services/archifaces.py:parse_baseline`, however, parses each non-comment line with `kind, family, path, n = raw.split("\t")`. For line 1, `raw.split("\t")` returns a one-element list, so the four-way unpack raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (got 1, expected 4)`. Any test that loads this committed baseline through `parse_baseline` (the ratchet comparison tests in `tests/test_arch_interfaces.py`) will therefore fail before comparing anything. The baseline format and the parser format are incompatible.
chunk_findings.title: tests/arch_baselines/arch_interfaces.txt:1

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts a wall-clock limit `time.monotonic() - started < 15` around `I.scan(ROOT)`. This is environment-dependent: on a cold page cache, first-run bytecode generation, a slow CI runner, or a loaded host, a correct implementation can exceed 15 seconds and cause a false failure. The prior reported finding still holds; nothing in this diff replaces the fixed threshold with a deterministic or hermetic check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:test_scan_is_cheap_enough_for_the_suite

chunk_findings.detail: The test scans the repository root and asserts `not grew` against the committed baseline, so it is not hermetic. An untracked scratch file under `ddflow/` containing any interface call, such as `ddflow/scratch.py` with `os.getenv("DEBUG")`, is picked up by `I.scan(ROOT)` and makes `grew` nonempty, failing the test even though the submitted code is correct. The same pollution can break the `ratchet == {"grew": [], ...}` assertion in `test_api_view_carries_interfaces_and_baseline_text`; the prior reported finding still holds.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:test_real_tree_ratchet_against_committed_baseline

chunk_findings.detail:
The new implementation splits the shell string on raw newlines before lexing and returns immediately when a fragment fails to tokenize, so it no longer respects quotes across newlines. For `subprocess.run("git commit -m 'a
b' && ls", shell=True)`, the first fragment `git commit -m 'a` raises `ValueError`, causing `_shell_commands` to return `["git"]`; the `&& ls` after the closing quote is never seen even though the shell runs both `git` and `ls`. The same newline split also invents commands in heredocs: `subprocess.run("cat <<EOF
ls
EOF", shell=True)` returns `["cat", "ls"]`, although `ls` is heredoc body, not a command. Thus the scanner both omits real CLI interfaces and fabricates false ones.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_keyword_arg` helper is defined in this diff but is never invoked anywhere in the file. `_call` remains the implementation previously reported, reading only `node.args[0]`. Keyword-only forms such as `subprocess.run(args=["git", "status"])`, `os.getenv(key="FOO")`, and `os.environ.get(key="FOO")` therefore still report family `<dynamic>` instead of the statically known name. The triage’s “probe fixed” does not answer this: this diff contains no change to `_call` that would use `_keyword_arg`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_call

chunk_findings.detail: The prose set adds `ast.JoinedStr` nodes only when the `ast.Expr` statement itself is a joined string (lines 141–146). A joined string used inside a list/tuple assignment is not an `ast.Expr`, so its child `Constant` nodes are not added to `self.prose`. With the default `literals=True`, the scan pass later visits each such `Constant` and calls `_literal_site`, so entries such as `MCP_METHODS = [f"tools/list"]` still produce protocol hits. The prior finding’s second half—f-string literal entries from `MCP_METHODS`/`ACP_METHODS`—therefore still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_Scan.__init__

chunk_findings.detail: The new redirection handling still misidentifies a command when a file descriptor precedes a redirection at the start of a command. For `subprocess.run("2>/dev/null git status", shell=True)`, shlex yields tokens roughly `["2", ">", "/dev/null", "git", "status"]`; `fresh` is still `True` when `"2"` is encountered, so `"2"` is appended as a program name and `"git"` is never recorded. The scanner then reports family `"2"` and fails to report the `git` interface, even though the actual first command is `git`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: `lex.commenters = ""` disables shlex comment handling for the whole rewritten line. Given `_shell_commands("# comment\ngit status")`, the helper turns the newline into `;`, then shlex yields tokens `#`, `comment`, `;`, `git`, `status`; because `fresh` is true at the start, the method returns `['#', 'git']`. In a shell the first line is only a comment and the only command is `git`, so the interface census records a bogus `#` interface.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The quote scanner treats a backslash-escaped quote as closing/opening a quoted region, but shell (and shlex) treats `\"` as a literal quote character. For the shell line `echo "a\"b"` followed by a newline and `ls` — i.e. the Python string value produced by `'echo "a\\"b"\nls'` — the helper closes the quoted region at the escaped quote, reopens it at the real closing quote, and therefore leaves the newline inside a quoted region instead of replacing it with `;`. shlex then sees no shell operator between `a"b` and `ls`, so `_shell_commands` returns `['echo']` and misses the `ls` command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_unquoted_newlines_to_semicolons

chunk_findings.detail: For the valid redirection `2>&1` placed before the command word, the new fd-guard only skips the `>`, and the bool `skip` consumes the following `&`; the `1` is then still parsed with `fresh == True`, so it is reported as a command. Given `subprocess.run("2>&1 git status", shell=True)`, shlex with `punctuation_chars=True` yields `["2", ">", "&", "1", "git", "status"]`; the function appends `"1"` instead of `"git"` and emits a false interface family `"1"`. The `2>/dev/null` case added in this change does not exercise the `>&` fd-duplication form.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The quote tracker does not handle backslash-escaped quotes outside quotes, so an unquoted newline after an escaped quote is not converted to a command separator. The shell line `echo \"hi` followed by a literal newline and then `ls` runs `echo` and `ls`, but the function sees the escaped `"` as opening a quote, leaves the newline in place, and shlex lexes it as one command; `_shell_commands` then returns only `["echo"]` and misses the external `ls` interface. This is reproducible from the Python literal `'echo \\"hi\nls'`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_unquoted_newlines_to_semicolons

chunk_findings.detail: The new shell-string branch returns `["sh"]` for any `shell=True` string command, so a statically known external CLI invocation such as `subprocess.run("git status", shell=True)` is recorded as the shell rather than as `git`. The census is intended to make external CLI tools (`git`, `gh`, `gitleaks`, harness CLIs, etc.) visible to the ratchet; this change makes a literal shell line invisible as the tool it actually runs. The claim that “no live site passes a literal line” is not enforced by the scanner: adding a source file containing `subprocess.run("git status", shell=True)` (or scanning a fixture/test source containing such a line) silently produces only an `sh` interface, so the ratchet can pass while bypassing the `git` adapter and defeating the stated “every external interface goes through its adapter” goal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:programs_of

chunk_findings.detail: The changed assertion makes the interface census deliberately ignore the external programs actually invoked by a shell string: the test source contains `os.system("git status && pre-commit run")`, but the expected program families are only `{"sh"}`. This is wrong for the stated census goal of counting CLI tools shelled to (git, gh, pre-commit, pip-audit, harness CLIs). For example, a module containing `os.system("pip-audit")` or `subprocess.run("git status", shell=True)` will now produce only a `sh` site, so the interface ratchet can pass even though `pip-audit`/`git` are invoked outside their adapters. The test itself demonstrates the undercount: the code runs `pre-commit`, yet the census is expected not to record `pre-commit`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:377

chunk_findings.detail: The new shell handling is only in the `ast.Constant` branch. For `subprocess.run(["git", "status"], shell=True)`, the first argument is an `ast.List`, so the unchanged list/tuple branch still returns `_head(e.elts[0])` — `"git"`. On POSIX, `subprocess` launches `/bin/sh` for that call (the sequence form supplies the shell command string as the first item, with later items as shell arguments), so the real immediate interface is the shell, and the scanner reports `git` instead of `sh`. This contradicts the new docstring (“for a shell call ... the program run is the shell”) and defeats the ratchet for direct shell use via the list form.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:programs_of

chunk_findings.detail: The diff changes the shell-call assertions so that `os.system("git status && pre-commit run")` and the other `os.system`/`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` cases now require the scanner to report only program family `"sh"` and no `"git"`, `"pre-commit"`, `"grep"`, `"uv"`, `"make"`, `"ls"`, etc. This codifies a scanner that no longer records the actual external programs named in shell command strings. Given the stated intent of this change — Census v2 must cover “CLI tools shelled to” (`git`, `gh`, `pre-commit`, `pip-audit`, harness CLIs, ...) so the guard can prove every external interface goes through its adapter — returning only `sh` makes `os.system("git status")` pass while the `git` interface is invisible, defeating the census for shelled CLIs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:377

chunk_findings.detail: The quote scanner treats a backslash-escaped quote as closing/opening a quoted region, but shell (and shlex) treats `\"` as a literal quote character. chunk_findings.detail: The new shell-string branch returns `["sh"]` for any `shell=True` string command, so a statically known external CLI invocation such as `subprocess.run("git status", shell=True)` is recorded as the shell rather than as `git`. The census is intended to make external CLI tools (`git`, `gh`, `gitleaks`, harness CLIs, etc.) visible to the ratchet; this change makes a literal shell line invisible as the tool it actually runs. The claim that “no live site passes a literal line” is not enforced by the scanner: adding a source file containing `subprocess.run("git status", shell=True)` (or scanning a fixture/test source containing such a line) silently produces only an `sh` interface, so the ratchet can pass while bypassing the `git` adapter and defeating the stated “every external interface goes through its adapter” goal.

chunk_findings.detail: The changed assertion makes the interface census deliberately ignore the external programs actually invoked by a shell string: the test source contains `os.system("git status && pre-commit run")`, but the expected program families are only `{"sh"}`. This is wrong for the stated census goal of counting CLI tools shelled to (git, gh, pre-commit, pip-audit, harness CLIs). chunk_findings.detail: The new shell handling is only in the `ast.Constant` branch. For `subprocess.run(["git", "status"], shell=True)`, the first argument is an `ast.List`, so the unchanged list/tuple branch still returns `_head(e.elts[0])` — `"git"`. On POSIX, `subprocess` launches `/bin/sh` for that call (the sequence form supplies the shell command string as the first item, with later items as shell arguments), so the real immediate interface is the shell, and the scanner reports `git` instead of `sh`. chunk_findings.detail: The diff changes the shell-call assertions so that `os.system("git status && pre-commit run")` and the other `os.system`/`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` cases now require the scanner to report only program family `"sh"` and no `"git"`, `"pre-commit"`, `"grep"`, `"uv"`, `"make"`, `"ls"`, etc. This codifies a scanner that no longer records the actual external programs named in shell command strings. chunk_findings.detail: The new shell-line matcher defines a “word” as `[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+`, which omits `_`. Because of that, identifiers containing an underscore are split and the first fragment can be mistaken for a known external program. For example, given `subprocess.run("rm -rf node_modules", shell=True)`, `_WORD.findall(e.value)` yields `["rm", "rf", "node", "modules"]`; since `node` is in `KNOWN_PROGRAMS`, `programs_of(..., shell=True)` returns `["sh", "node"]`. The shell line does not invoke `node`—it invokes `rm`—but the census records an external `node` interface, which can spuriously require a `node` adapter or make the interface ratchet grow. The same over-reporting occurs for common shell strings such as `$git_status` or `gh_token`.

chunk_findings.detail: The added `_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+")` uses the module-level name `re`, but this change does not add `import re` to `archifaces_scan.py`. At module import time Python evaluates this line and raises `NameError: name 're' is not defined`, so `ddflow.services.archifaces_scan` fails to import. Because `ddflow/services/archifaces.py` imports `AGENT_CLIS`, `PLATFORM`, and `TOOLS` from this module, `ddflow.services.archifaces` also fails to import, breaking the interface census before any scan can run.

Because of that, identifiers containing an underscore are split and the first fragment can be mistaken for a known external program. For example, given `subprocess.run("rm -rf node_modules", shell=True)`, `_WORD.findall(e.value)` yields `["rm", "rf", "node", "modules"]`; since `node` is in `KNOWN_PROGRAMS`, `programs_of(..., shell=True)` returns `["sh", "node"]`. The shell line does not invoke `node`—it invokes `rm`—but the census records an external `node` interface, which can spuriously require a `node` adapter or make the interface ratchet grow. The same over-reporting occurs for common shell strings such as `$git_status` or `gh_token`.

chunk_findings.detail: The added `_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+")` uses the module-level name `re`, but this change does not add `import re` to `archifaces_scan.py`. At module import time Python evaluates this line and raises `NameError: name 're' is not defined`, so `ddflow.services.archifaces_scan` fails to import. Because `ddflow/services/archifaces.py` imports `AGENT_CLIS`, `PLATFORM`, and `TOOLS` from this module, `ddflow.services.archifaces` also fails to import, breaking the interface census before any scan can run.

chunk_findings.detail: `_shell_commands` lists newline as a shell operator in `_SHELL_OPS`, but the shlex configuration used above it never emits newline as a token: [REDACTED] punctuation_chars=True)` with `whitespace_split=True` treats newline as whitespace and skips it. Given `os.system("git status\npre-commit run")`, the token stream is effectively `git`, `status`, `pre-commit`, `run`; `git` sets `fresh=False`, and because no newline operator resets `fresh`, `pre-commit` is not returned. `programs_of` then records only program `git`, missing the second external program run by the same shell command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The shell-operator table treats `&` as a command separator, but shlex with `punctuation_chars=True` tokenizes redirections such as `2>&1` into separate `2`, `>`, `&`, and `1` tokens. Since `>` is not in `_SHELL_OPS` but `&` is, the `&` in `>&` resets `fresh`, and the following `1` is appended as if it were the next command. For `os.system("git status > /dev/null 2>&1")`, the scanner records a bogus `program` site for family `1`, a false external interface that can make the ratchet fail on code that only redirects file descriptors.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The test is presented as the safety argument for excluding `I.SELF_MODULES` from the interface census, but it only checks static import families. The interface census counts managed-file literals without requiring an import (for example `g = "AGENTS.md"` is counted in `test_managed_files_exclude_prose_and_comments`). If someone adds `open("AGENTS.md").read()` to `ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py`, the interface census will suppress the resulting site because the module is self-excluded, while `A.scan(ROOT)` gains no `subprocess`, `http`, `shutil`, `clock-env`, `sqlite3`, or `fsio` importer for that module because `open` is a builtin. `test_the_census_modules_import_no_os_family` and `test_the_census_does_not_count_its_own_pattern_tables` therefore still pass even though an external managed-file interface has been hidden from the census.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:test_the_census_modules_import_no_os_family

chunk_findings.detail: The prose exclusion is broken: `self.prose = {id(n.value) ...}` stores the identity of the string value, but both `file_protocols` and the `ast.Constant` branch test `id(node) not in self.prose`, the identity of the AST node. Those two IDs are never equal. A docstring `"""https://example.com"""` therefore reaches `_literal_site` and emits `network host:example.com`, and a docstring exactly `"tools/list"` still leaks into `file_protocols`. This is previous finding 6 still present, not fixed by the cited probe.

`_SHELL_OPS` contains `"
"`, but `shlex.shlex(..., whitespace_split=True)` consumes newline as whitespace, so `"
"` is never returned as a token. For `os.system("git status
pre-commit run")`, the token list is `["git", "status", "pre-commit", "run"]`; `_shell_commands` returns only `["git"]`, so `pre-commit` is run but not recorded. This underreports a newline-separated external program.

chunk_findings.detail: `shutil.which("git")` is recorded as a `program` site, but `shutil.which` only locates an executable; it does not run it. Given `if shutil.which("git"): ...` with no subprocess call, the scanner emits `program git`, a false dependency that can make the arch guard fail even though no git process is ever run.

chunk_findings.detail: `_git_hooks_join` flattens every `ast.Div` BinOp without requiring a path constructor. Valid code with a user-defined `__truediv__` such as `NonPath() / ".git" / "hooks"` leaves `[None, ".git", "hooks"]`, so `pairwise` finds `(".git", "hooks")` and emits a `managed-file` site for `.git/hooks` although no local path is constructed. This false positive can fail the arch guard.

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `I.scan(ROOT)` completes in under 15 seconds of wall-clock time. This makes the suite fail based on machine load, disk speed, or CI virtualization even when the scanner's performance has not regressed and the change is correct. For example, on a shared or throttled CI worker with a cold page cache, the full-repository parse and scan can exceed 15 s, causing a spurious failure unrelated to scanner behavior.

chunk_findings.detail:
The newline fix splits the raw shell line on `
` before shlex, so it treats newlines that are not shell command separators as separators. For `subprocess.run("cat <<EOF
git status
EOF", shell=True)`, the heredoc body line `git status` is lexed with `fresh=True`, so `pre-commit`-style logic records `git` as an external program even though the shell only passes that text to `cat`; this creates a bogus `program` interface. The same split also mis-handles shell line continuation: `subprocess.run("git status \
pre-commit run", shell=True)` is one `git` command with `pre-commit` as an argument, but the scanner records `pre-commit` as a separate command. Conversely, `subprocess.run("git commit -m 'line1
line2' && pre-commit run", shell=True)` makes the first split line unbalanced for shlex; the function returns after `git` and never sees the real `pre-commit` command. Thus the census can both invent and miss external interfaces for multi-line shell strings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: `shlex(..., punctuation_chars=True)` tokenizes parentheses as separate tokens, but `_SHELL_OPS` does not treat `(` or `)` as command boundaries. For `subprocess.run("(git status)", shell=True)`, the token stream begins with `(`; because `fresh` is true, `_shell_commands` returns `(` as a program and then ignores `git` since `fresh` is now false. If unknown tokens are counted, the ratchet sees a bogus external program `(`; if unknown tokens are filtered, the real `git` dependency is missed. This is wrong for a shell line where the actual external command inside the subshell is `git`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The new `literals=False` path suppresses every string-literal interface kind in census modules, not only their pattern tables. The added test demonstrates the suppression directly: in `services/archifaces_scan.py`, `X = "AGENTS.md"` produces no `managed-file` site (only the `env`/`REAL` call site is kept), while the same literal in `services/real.py` is counted. Therefore, if a census module contains a real literal interface—e.g. `AGENTS = "AGENTS.md"` later used to read the file, a default protocol method literal, or a default URL host—the interface census omits it solely because the module is in `I.SELF_MODULES`. The delta only proves that env call sites survive; real literal interfaces inside census modules remain invisible to the ratchet, so the previous self-exclusion hole is not fully answered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:sites_in

chunk_findings.detail: The new `literals=False` mode is meant to hide the census modules' own pattern tables, but it suppresses every string-literal interface kind in those modules, including a genuine `managed-file` use. The new probe in `tests/test_arch_interfaces.py::test_the_census_does_not_count_its_own_pattern_tables` only proves an `env` call survives for a self module; it does not exercise the previous managed-file scenario. Given `ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py` containing `open("AGENTS.md").read()`, that module is in `I.SELF_MODULES` and is scanned with `literals=False`, so the `AGENTS.md` managed-file literal is omitted, `I.scan(ROOT)` reports no site, and the arch guard can pass even though a census module reaches a managed file directly. This is previous finding 3 still present: the fix/probe does not answer the suppressed-managed-file path, only the suppressed-call path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:sites_in literals=False

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_unquoted_newlines_to_semicolons` removes newlines before shlex, but the lexer is still constructed with shlex's default `commenters = '#'`. Given `os.system("ls # comment\ngit status")`, the helper produces `ls # comment ; git status`; shlex treats everything from `#` to the end of the string as a comment, so `_shell_commands` returns only `ls` and the scanner omits the `git` program. In a real shell the comment ends at the newline and `git status` runs, so this underreports an external interface.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The helper treats any unquoted newline as a command separator, but a backslash-newline outside quotes is a shell line continuation, not a separator. For the shell string produced by `os.system("git \\\nstatus")` (characters `git \` newline `status`), the helper changes it to `git \ ; status`; `_shell_commands` then sees `;` as an operator and returns both `git` and `status`. The shell joins the continuation and runs only `git status`, so the scanner emits a false `program status` dependency.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_unquoted_newlines_to_semicolons

chunk_findings.detail: The manual comment state introduced by `lex.commenters = ""` ends a comment at any `;` token, but a semicolon inside a shell comment does not end the comment. Given `os.system("# note ; git status")`, the shell treats the whole line as a comment and runs no program. The scanner tokenizes this as `#`, `note`, `;`, `git`, `status`; the `#` starts its comment state, the `;` ends that state, and `git` is returned as a program family. This creates a false external interface and can make the interface ratchet fail on code that runs nothing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The comment state also starts a comment from any token beginning with `#`, even when the `#` is quoted, and the pre-pass does not know that shell comments ignore quotes. For `os.system('echo "# note" && git status')`, the shell runs `echo` and then `git`, but shlex yields the argument token `# note`; `_shell_commands` enters comment mode there and, because there is no `;` token, never records `git`. For `os.system("# it's\nls")`, the shell comment ends at the newline and runs `ls`, but the helper treats the apostrophe as opening a quote, leaves the newline inside that quote, shlex then sees an unbalanced quote, and the fallback returns only `#`, so `ls` is missed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: `line.replace("\\\n", " ")` removes every backslash-newline pair without counting preceding backslashes, so it treats an escaped backslash followed by a newline as a line continuation. For an unquoted shell string whose value is `git ` followed by two literal backslashes, a newline, and `pre-commit run`, the shell sees `\\` as a literal backslash argument to `git` and the following newline as a command separator, so `pre-commit` runs. The helper replaces the second backslash and newline with a space, removing the separator, so `_shell_commands` returns only `git` and the census misses the `pre-commit` external interface.
